title: Type it like a local
blurb: Two characters of very common courtesy. 🇹🇼⌨️

title: Dos teclados, un mensaje
blurb: No keyboard picture this time, and the digits do not all mean the same thing.

title: The Key Right of the Space Bar
blurb: Nobody pressed the key to the right of the space bar.

title: Mother Tongue
blurb: Открытка из Москвы, typed on a PC. Every word but one; that one insisted on being typed in its mother tongue.

title: A Friend from Afar
blurb: The Master said it. Seoul recites it. One word came from even farther away.

title: Every Key a Shape
blurb: 日月金木水火土. Seven characters; every letter on this keyboard stands for a shape.

title: A Question from Hanoi
blurb: Typed in Hanoi with Telex: a question, and a borrowed phrase. One Vietnamese sentence, but not every syllable in it is Vietnamese. Keep the borrowed phrase as it was typed: it is part of the answer.

title: One Handover
blurb: The keyboard of #1 has a twin in Taipei. One passed the message to the other, once. The line comes from a hillside town nearby.

title: Metal and Orchids
blurb: 易經. The second line was typed in a hurry. Two lines, eight characters each.

title: Digits, Three Ways
blurb: Greek first. Then three keyboards on which a digit means three different things. An English message: most of it went through Greek, and each of its last three words through a keyboard of its own.

title: The Key You Carried
blurb: This one came without a key. You have been carrying it: one number from each of #7 to #11, in order. Five characters, two keys each, on a keyboard of #10.
